metadata.title: Holly Farms Corp. v. NLRB, 517 U.S. 392 (1996) (No. 95-210)
metadata.creator: Supreme Court of the United States
metadata.description:
Case name: Holly Farms Corp. v. NLRB

Opinion filed: 1996-05-13

Docket No.: 95-210

Citations:
• 134 L. Ed. 2d 593
• 116 S. Ct. 1396
• 517 U.S. 392
• 1996 U.S. LEXIS 2801

Case holding summaries:
• “Courts, in turn, must respect the judgment of the agency empowered to apply the law • employer conceded that truck drivers who transported chickens and crews between farms and processing plant did not perform activities “on a farm”
• "Primary farming includes the raising of poultry."
• "Courts, in turn, must respect the judgment of the agency empowered to apply the law 'to varying fact patterns' even if the issue 'with nearly equal reason [might] be resolved one way rather than another'."
• stating that reasonable NLRB interpretations of the Act must be upheld even if they are not "the best way to read the statute" (emphasis omitted)
• when agency administrator chooses among conflicting reasonable interpretations, reviewing courts must respect the agency’s judgment
• holding that terms connected by a disjunctive are to be given separate meanings
• "Courts, in turn, must respect the judgment of the agency empowered to apply the law 'to varying fact patterns' even if the issue 'with nearly equal reason [might] be resolved one way rather than another'."
• "For the Board to prevail, it need not show that its construction is the best way to read the statute; rather, courts must respect the Board's judgment so long as its reading is a reasonable one."
• deferring to the Board’s decision that certain workers were not “agricultural laborer[s]” and were therefore eligible to unionize under the Act
• "For the Board to prevail, it need not show that its construction is the best way to read the statute; rather, courts must respect the Board's judgment so long as its reading is a reasonable one."
• deferring to the Board’s decision that certain workers were not “agricultural laborer[s]” and were therefore eligible to unionize under the Act
• "The deference owed to an expert tribunal cannot be allowed to slip into a judicial inertia ..."
• "It is well settled that exemptions from the Fair Labor Standards Act are to be narrowly construed."
• exemptions from the FLSA "are to be narrowly construed against the employers seeking to assert them"
• "Reviewing courts are not obliged to stand aside and rubber-stamp their affirmance of administrative decisions that they deem inconsistent with a statutory mandate or that frustrate the congressional policy underlying a statute"
• secondary farming embraces "any practices, whether or not themselves farming practices, which are performed either by a farmer or on a farm, incidently to or in conjunction with `such' farming operations"
• "we will uphold any interpretation [of the term `employee' in NLRA § 2(3)] that is reasonably defensible"
• suggesting that courts should defer to any reasonable interpretation of the jurisdictional provisions of the NLRA by the NLRB
